newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai current account, trade data positive -BOT.
newsitem.headline: Thai current account, trade data positive -BOT.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Thursday released positive preliminary trade and current account deficit figures for November 1996 but said the country's balance of payments posted a deficit for the second month in a row.

The central bank's chief economist, Kleothong Hetrakul, told reporters that Thailand's current account deficit for November narrowed sharply to 21.7 bln baht, the lowest since September 1995 when the deficit was 16.9 billion baht.
The deficit was 30.2 billion baht in October 1996.

Kleothong said that the November trade deficit also narrowed sharply to 24.2 billion baht, the lowest since September 1995 when the deficit was 10.4 billion baht. The figure for last October was 36.2 billion baht.

However, Thailand registered a 19.2 billion baht monthly deficit in its balance of payments account for December, sharply higher than the 6.2 billion baht deficit posted in November, and a surplus of 10 billion recorded in October, she added.
The much higher December balance of payments deficit could be attributed to temporary and seasonal year-end factors such as annual repatriation of funds by foreign firms, she said.
It could also be due to restrictive central bank measures implemented early last year to slow down inflows of short-term funds into the country, she added.
However, the economist was confident that the balance of payments deficit would normalise in January and end the year in a surplus.
